name: Promptfoo
tagline: MCP-Native Agent Eval vs Config-Driven CLI Eval and Red-Teaming
oneLine: An open-source CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps; evals run on your machine from declarative test configs.
tldrVendor: Promptfoo is an open-source CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps. Evals run on your machine and talk directly with the LLM, with results in a local web viewer.

rows.vendor: Open-source CLI and Node library driven by declarative YAML test cases; also runs in CI/CD.
rows.quote: promptfoo is an open-source CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps.

rows.vendor: Runs locally; a basic Docker image hosts a server that stores evals (SQLite); not recommended for production.
rows.quote: Promptfoo provides a basic Docker image that allows you to host a server that stores evals.

rows.vendor: No in-app instrumentation; evals run on your machine and call the LLM directly. The Enterprise MCP Proxy is in-path.
rows.quote: This software runs completely locally. The evals run on your machine and talk directly with the LLM.

rows.vendor: Deterministic assertions plus model-graded (LLM rubric) assertions; custom JavaScript and Python assertions.
rows.quote: These metrics are programmatic tests that are run on LLM output.

rows.vendor: A cost assertion checks provider-reported cost against a threshold; requires the provider to return cost information.
rows.quote: The cost assertion checks whether the cost reported by the selected provider is at or below a specified threshold.

rows.vendor: MCP provider tests MCP servers directly; ships an MCP server exposing its eval tools; Enterprise MCP Proxy product.
rows.quote: The mcp provider allows you to use Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers directly as providers in promptfoo.

rows.vendor: Open-source core is MIT licensed; Promptfoo Enterprise (hosted SaaS) and Enterprise On-Prem are commercial.
rows.quote: Promptfoo remains open source and MIT licensed.

rows.vendor: Announced 2026-03-09 that it agreed to be acquired by OpenAI; its about page states Promptfoo is now part of OpenAI.
rows.quote: Today we are announcing that Promptfoo has agreed to be acquired by OpenAI.

rows.vendor: Local web viewer opens eval results in the browser; results can be shared to promptfoo.app or a self-hosted server.
rows.quote: After running an eval, view results in your browser: npx promptfoo@latest view

rows.vendor: Providers for OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Google, HuggingFace, local models, HTTP, custom JS/Python scripts, MCP, n8n.
rows.quote: Use OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Google, HuggingFace, open-source models like Llama, or integrate custom API providers

rows.vendor: Prompts inline or in Git-tracked files; external stores (Langfuse, Portkey, Helicone) referenced by version or label.
rows.quote: Store prompts in external files for better organization

rows.vendor: Enterprise tier lists SSO, granular permission profiles, RBAC and teams; site shows SOC2 and ISO 27001 badges.

vendorReasons.text: You need red-teaming probes and vulnerability scanning of your LLM app alongside evals.
You need declarative YAML test cases that run as a CLI step in CI/CD and compare models side-by-side.
You need evals that run entirely on your machine and talk directly to the LLM, with no server.
You need a proxy that governs which MCP servers your organization's applications and users may reach.
You need an on-premises enterprise deployment with a dedicated runner behind your firewall.

faq.question: What is the difference between Iris and Promptfoo?
faq.vendorPart: Promptfoo is an open-source CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps: tests are declared in config, run locally against the LLM, and viewed in a local web viewer.

faq.question: Is Iris better than Promptfoo for MCP agent evaluation?
faq.vendorPart: Promptfoo offers red-teaming and vulnerability scanning, side-by-side model comparison across many providers, and an enterprise MCP Proxy that controls which MCP servers an organization can reach.
